page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top centre. Page number at the top left. Catchword at the bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: pitudines, fac ut in nos ipsos severe agamus, & ab Animis nostris Reformatio incipiat, ut perspicaci Iudicio, & integro Corde accedentes, quae in Ecclesia aut Statu perperam facta sunt, idonei simus reformare.
Cor mundum crea in Nobis Deus & Spiritum rectum innova in visceribus nostris, ut tuo ductu simul & tua Benedictione in Tuam omnia Gloriam faciamus.
Miserere deformitatum & vulnerum, quae temerarii & saevi Reformatores huic Ecclesiae & Statui inflixerunt; exstingue Factionum flammas sub praetextu Reformandi accensas.

Et quemadmodum per haec mutuo dissidia, & confusiones palam omnibus facere voluisti quam sint pravi nonnullorum fines; & infirma Iudicia; ita ex his flammis educas nos purgationes, praeeunte Christiana magis, & plus in se charitatis habente Reformatione, ubi nihil vindictae aut ambitus, avaritiae denique aut sacrilegii polleat in eorum consilia, quibus opus tam insigne & bonum, & jam maxime necessarium aequo & licito more peragendum providentia tua demandaverit; ut internae pietatis felicitate auctiti ego simul & populus etiam Pacis externa beneficio rectius nobis[?] in posterum discamus.

page.notes: The bottom right shows "21.De", large type, which opens the next section; it is treated as a catchword. The word before "in posterum" at the end is partly obscured and reads as "nobis"; uncertain, marked [?]. The word "auctiti" is partly unclear and may be "auctifi"; the reading is uncertain. Long s in "fac" and "faciamus" is read as the word itself. The running head is Greek transliterated into Latin capitals, copied as printed.
